content: Nabumetone, a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke compared to individuals who do not take NSAIDs. These cardiovascular events can occur without warning and may result in death. The risk is higher for those who use NSAIDs for extended periods. Inform your doctor if you or your family have a history of heart disease, heart attack, or stroke, if you smoke, or if you have high cholesterol, high blood pressure, or diabetes. Seek emergency medical attention immediately if you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side of the body, or slurred speech. Do not take nabumetone immediately before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. NSAIDs, including nabumetone, can cause ulcers, bleeding, or perforations in the stomach or intestines, which may occur at any time during treatment, often without warning, and can be fatal. The risk is higher for long-term users, older adults, those in poor health, or individuals who consume large amounts of alcohol while taking nabumetone. Notify your doctor if you are taking anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), aspirin, other NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), or oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, prednisone). Also, inform your doctor if you have a history of ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, or other bleeding disorders. Stop taking nabumetone and contact your doctor if you experience stomach pain, heartburn, vomiting blood or material resembling coffee grounds, blood in the stool, or black, tarry stools. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor will monitor your symptoms and may order tests to assess your response to nabumetone. Communicate how you are feeling to ensure the medication is prescribed at the lowest effective dose to minimize serious side effects. Your doctor or pharmacist will provide a Medication Guide when you start nabumetone and with each prescription refill. Read the information carefully and ask questions if needed. You can also visit the FDA website for the Medication Guide. Nabumetone is prescribed to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It works by inhibiting the production of substances in the body that cause pain, fever, and inflammation. Nabumetone is available as an oral tablet, typically taken once or twice daily, with or without food, at the same time(s) each day. Follow your prescription instructions carefully and do not take more or less than directed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Before taking nabumetone, inform your doctor if you are allergic to nabumetone, aspirin, other NSAIDs, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Mention medications such as ACE inhibitors, diuretics, lithium, oral diabetes medications, phenytoin, and methotrexate, as your doctor may need to adjust doses or monitor for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have asthma, especially if accompanied by frequent nasal congestion or polyps, swelling in the extremities, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, particularly in the last trimester, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking nabumetone, contact your doctor immediately. Inform your healthcare provider if you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, as nabumetone may need to be discontinued. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged sun exposure, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as nabumetone may increase skin sensitivity to sunlight. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for the next dose. Do not double doses to make up for a missed one. Nabumetone may cause minor side effects, including diarrhea, constipation, gas, bloating, dizziness, headache, dry mouth, mouth sores, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, increased sweating, or ringing in the ears. Notify your doctor if these symptoms persist or worsen. Serious side effects include unexpected weight gain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, fatigue, loss of appetite, upper right abdominal pain, flu-like symptoms, fever, blisters, rash, itching, hives, swelling of the face or extremities, difficulty breathing or swallowing, hoarseness, pale skin, rapid heartbeat, cloudy or bloody urine, back pain, or painful urination. Stop taking nabumetone and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Report serious side effects to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store nabumetone in its original container, tightly closed, out of reach of children, at room temperature, and away from excess heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual collapses or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include fatigue, drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, difficulty breathing, seizures, or coma. Do not share nabumetone with others. Consult your pharmacist with any questions about refilling your prescription.
